# Enemy force fields scale with level progression

**Headline:** Add data-driven enemy force fields that appear from a per-archetype
start level (some enemies shielded from level 2, others later) and grow stronger
with each level, absorbing a number of player hits before the ship inside is
exposed and destroyed as normal.

## Problem statement

Deeper campaign levels currently raise threat only through raw enemy density and
firepower; each regular enemy is still a single-hit (or fixed 5-hit) target. The
result is that upgraded weapons trivialise late-level fodder. Adding a
**force-field layer** — a distinct, readable barrier that absorbs several hits
before the ship inside becomes vulnerable — gives the late campaign a new
escalation axis that existing durability (`EnemyConfig.health`) does not provide,
without touching weapon/power-up economies.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want enemies in deeper levels to absorb a few hits behind a
  visible barrier, so late-game firepower is challenged again and reading a
  shielded enemy (barrier first, hull second) is intuitive.
- **As a balance engineer**, I want force-field strength (which archetypes are
  shielded, from which level, and how the field's hit count grows) to be
  data-driven and tunable per enemy, so I can shape difficulty without scene
  code.
- **As a developer**, I want the force-field logic to live once in the shared
  core so the game and every gym behave identically, with no divergent copies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data-driven per-archetype fields.** New `EnemyConfig` fields
  `forceFieldStartLevel` (campaign level at which this archetype first gains a
  field; `0` = never shielded), `forceFieldStartHits` (field hits when it
  appears) and `forceFieldMaxHits` (field hits at the campaign maximum level)
  are added to the CSV schema/codec, config types and seed defaults, each
  defaulting so that **every existing enemy is unshielded at level 1** and the
  shipped campaign is behaviourally unchanged until at least level 2. Field
  strength at any level is `clamp(round(lerp(startHits @ startLevel → maxHits @
  10)), 0, 5)` via a pure, Phaser-free shared resolver. Heavier archetypes
  (Tank/Harvester) carry higher base values than light ones.
- **AC2 — Force-field absorbs hits before the hull.** A shielded enemy survives
  its fleet of field hits first; each absorbed hit consumes the bullet (with
  feedback) but does **not** decrement `EnemyConfig.health`. Only after the
  field is broken does the enemy's normal health apply (so most archetypes die
  on the next hit; the 5-HP Harvester still needs 5). Every player damage source
  (normal bullet, piercing, AOE weapons, Smart Bomb, Orbital Strike, Frenzy
  bonus hits) depletes the field through the existing shared `takeDamage()`
  seam — no parallel damage path. Player contact/ram: a shielded enemy's field
  absorbs the ram — exactly one field hit is consumed, the enemy survives, the
  player survives the collision and is not destroyed. Once the field is down,
  the existing contact rule applies unchanged (both destroyed,
  AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT). The absorb must be one field hit per ram contact, not
  per overlapping frame (documented re-arm, mirroring the Thorn Field ram
  absorption in `CombatScene._handleCollisions` step 4).
- **AC3 — Readable feedback.** Shielded enemies render a shared bubble drawn by
  the `CombatEffectVisuals` helper family, visually distinct from the player's
  Shield and Force Field bubbles; each absorbed hit triggers the existing shared
  impact feedback; the breaking hit runs a distinct break flash/audio cue.
- **AC4 — Gym parity and tunability.** The same resolver drives the game
  (`PlayScene` spawn path, run level from `WaveManager`) and the level gym
  (`GymLevel`), with a parity test. The enemy-config gym editor
  (`GymFodderEnemies` slider surface) gains force-field controls so a
  formation-gym (no campaign context) spawn can force a field on with a given
  hit count; the divergence (gym slider sets hits directly instead of a level
  curve) is recorded in the code and this item.
- **AC5 — Verification and documentation.** Unit tests cover the resolver curve
  (start level, ramp, clamping, cap, L1-unchanged), CSV codec defaults, entity
  absorb/break behaviour, and scene integration; game↔gym parity test passes;
  the duplicate-body guard stays green; a bot-batch evidence run at L1/L5/L10
  records `survivalSeconds`, `levelReached`, `avoidableHits` and
  `enemiesKilledByArchetype` before/after (or demonstrates the field keeps the
  campaign playable). GDD §2.6 (remove "no shield layer"), §4.1 and
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` are updated with the new behaviour
  and tuning table; **all related documentation is updated** and the **full
  project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity is mandatory** (repo `AGENTS.md`): enabled gameplay
  behaviour is shared code consumed by the game and every relevant gym; only a
  documented disabled feature may diverge. The force-field resolver and bubble
  helper must live in the shared core, not per-scene copies.
- **Level 1 is untouched.** Defaults guarantee zero shielded enemies at level 1,
  preserving onboarding, tests and the existing balance baseline.
- **No changes to enemy `health`, weapon/power-up economies, or the player
  Force Field / Shield power-ups.** Fields are a new, additive layer.
- **Backwards-compatible config persistence** — existing enemy config blobs and
  the CSV load with the new fields defaulted (`0`); no schema break.
- **Determinism** — field strength is a pure function of (level, config); same
  level + seed ⇒ identical shields, so the fixed/curve campaign determinism
  contract is preserved.
- **No new player-facing UI** beyond the in-game bubble and gym editor controls.

## Existing state

- Regular-enemy health is data-driven (`EnemyConfig.health`, default 1; Harvester
  5 HP) and applied via `BaseEnemy.takeDamage()` — the shared damage seam every
  damage source already routes through (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`:
  bullet, piercing, AOE, Smart Bomb, Orbital Strike, Frenzy).
- `EnemyConfig` is CSV-backed (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) with a numeric
  codec (`src/core/csv.ts`), seed defaults (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`) and a
  **gym enemy editor** slider surface (`GymFodderEnemies.ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES`).
- Spawn seam: `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` → `loadEnemyConfig(key)` →
  `createEnemyFromConfig`; the run level is available via `WaveManager.level`.
  `GymLevel` launches real campaign waves through the same factory.
- The **player** has Shield (absorbs hits) and Gradius-style Force Field
  (reflects bullets) power-ups; neither has any enemy-side counterpart. GDD
  §2.6 currently states "no shield layer", which this feature deliberately
  changes.
- Level-scaling work is in flight (epic AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P): its contract tests
  (AH-0MVLJCYGW001TRB3) are done; the `src/core/levelScaling.ts` implementation
  (`AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X`) is pending.

## Desired change

1. Add `forceFieldStartLevel` / `forceFieldStartHits` / `forceFieldMaxHits` to
   `EnemyConfig` (types, CSV codec, seed defaults, CSV rows; default 0/1/1).
2. Add a pure resolver (proposed `src/core/enemyForceField.ts`,
   `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)`); coordinate reuse of
   `levelScaling.ts` plumbing if F1 (AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X) has landed.
3. Thread the resolved field hits into entity spawn (game and level gym through
   the shared factory/config path) and implement field state + bubble in
   `BaseEnemy` (draw, absorb decrement, break effects); keep `takeDamage()`
   consuming the field before `health`. Add the **ram-absorb branch** to
   `CombatScene._handleCollisions` step 4 (one field hit per ram contact,
   player and enemy both survive; falls through to the existing both-destroyed
   rule once the field is down) — shared, so the game and every gym inherit it.
4. Add the shared bubble/break visuals to `CombatEffectVisuals` and any new SFX
   cue to the audio registry; add the gym-editor force-field sliders.
5. Tests: TDD contract tests for the resolver/codec/entity, game↔gym parity,
   and a bot-batch evidence run at L1/L5/L10.
6. Update GDD §2.6/§4.1 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; refresh
   the enemy-config CSV header comments.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — Add `forceFieldStartLevel`, `forceFieldStartHits`, `forceFieldMaxHits` to `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` + `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — Seed defaults and per-archetype values (`0` default = never/unchanged).
- `src/core/csv.ts` — Numeric codec support for the new columns (default 0).
- `src/core/enemyForceField.ts` — **New** pure resolver `enemyForceFieldHits(level, config)` (curve, clamp, cap 5, L1 = 0).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — Field state, bubble draw, absorb-before-health in `takeDamage()`, break feedback, ram-absorb entry point.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` (+ `CombatScene.test.ts`) — Ram-absorb branch in `_handleCollisions` step 4 with the shared re-arm, mirroring `tryConsumeThornsRam`. Note: this file is **shared core**, so the change lands once for the game and all gyms.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Thread effective field hits into entity construction from config.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Resolve and pass field hits at spawn (run level via `WaveManager`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` (+ `GymBotTuning`/`GymCurveSequencer` if they spawn campaign waves) — same resolver for parity.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — Force-field sliders/controls on the enemy-config editor (documented divergence: direct hits, no level curve).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` (+ tests) — Shared enemy-force-field bubble + break flash helper.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Any field-break cue (reuse existing cues where possible).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — Game↔gym parity block stays green.
- `src/core/*.test.ts`, `src/entities/BaseEnemy.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/*.test.ts` — Resolver, codec, entity, integration tests.
- `src/ai/eval/` + `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — Bot-batch evidence mode at L1/L5/L10 (extend the F5 per-level harness if landed).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Behaviour + tuning table.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P** (in-progress epic) — Level-scaled enemy counts / power-up drops; the level-scaling infrastructure (`levelScaling.ts`, F1 AH-0MVLJEE7O008RX9X) that this feature coordinates with.
- **AH-0MUI820PM0038HS2** (completed) — Harvester + data-driven multi-hit `health`; the seam this feature extends.
- **AH-0MUJRVYWG006NJUU** (completed) — Shared multi-hit kill finalisation / `takeDamage` seam.
- **AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR** (completed) — Data-driven enemy health config (CSV codec + editor).
- **AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT** (completed) — Contact rule: player crashing into an enemy destroys both. **Extended by this item** (Q6 = B): a shielded enemy's field absorbs the ram (one field hit, both survive); unshielded enemies keep the original rule.
- **AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14** (open) — Player Force Field feedback (distinct scope; do not conflate).
- **AH-0MV97RISJ002WR2S** (open) — Wave Laser limited hit power (piercing interplay; verify AOE/piercing behaviour against the field).
- Repo `AGENTS.md` — Gym↔game parity convention.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7USMWN0071UF5** – Clarify enemy pass-through and bullet-blocking rules in GDD (Wall vs Dive Bomb) (completed)
- **AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14** – More forcefield feedback (open)
- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** – Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K' (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: destroyed, enemies, exposed, fields, force (+13 more); the enemy-build/health seams this feature extends
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: the GDD §2.6/§4.1 floor the "no shield layer" rule this item changes
- `README.md` — matched: broad gameplay terms; check for any shield/level claims on release

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** the three-field linear model (start level, start hits, max hits at L10) is the right "per-enemy curve variation" shape; operator confirmed per-enemy tunable start levels (some L2, others L3+) and "subtle variations of this curve for different enemies".
- **Assumption:** "killed in a single hit" after field break applies to the 1-HP majority; the Harvester keeps its 5 HP once its field is down (AC2, operator Q2 = A).
- **Assumption (confirmed, Q6 = B):** a shielded enemy's field also absorbs a player **contact/ram** — exactly one field hit is consumed and both sides survive the collision; the pre-existing rule (both destroyed, AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT) applies once the field is down.
- **Assumption (implementation detail, flagged):** "one field hit per ram" needs a re-arm so a sustained overlap cannot drain the whole field frame-by-frame. Proposed: a documented ram re-arm cooldown (~0.5 s) resolved once in the shared core; recorded as an OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix for the review gate.
- **Risk:** force fields stack with the level-scaling density/drop changes (epic AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P) and could push late levels into bullet-sink tedium; mitigated by the 5-hit cap, per-archetype defaults, and bot-batch survival evidence.
- **Risk:** heavy archetypes (Tank/Harvester) with fields at L2–3 may frustrate players who maxed weapons; mitigated by keeping light archetypes unshielded for longer and tuning via CSV.
- **Risk:** the gym slider for formation gyms bypasses the level curve, so an editor could author values the campaign never produces; documented divergence + editorial note in the gym panel.
- **Risk:** editing the CSV schema/editor touches shared tooling (codec, gym panel, docs tests); keep defaults `0` so existing rows and persisted blobs load unchanged.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no retuning of enemy health, weapon levels, drop rates or the player shield/force-field power-ups; separate items are created for any of those discovered during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers


- **Q6 — Should a shielded enemy absorb a player ram with its field, or is contact unchanged (both destroyed) as AC2 originally stated?** Options: (A) unchanged — ram destroys both regardless of field; (B) field absorbs the ram — one field hit is consumed and the player survives the collision; (C) field breaks entirely on ram, enemy survives, player destroyed. — **Answer (operator): B.** Source: interactive reply to the plan skill. A shielded enemy's field absorbs the ram: one field hit is consumed, the enemy survives and the player survives the collision. Once the field is down the original contact rule (both destroyed, AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT) applies. AC2 and the Risks section were rewritten accordingly. Precedent reused: Thorn Field's ram absorption (`tryConsumeThornsRam`) in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` step 4 of `_handleCollisions`.
- **OPEN QUESTION (Q6 follow-on, for the producer at the plan review gate):** how long is the ram re-arm after a field absorbs a ram? Without one, a held overlap consumes a field hit every frame and drains the field instantly. **Recommended:** a dedicated ~0.5 s shared re-arm constant (do *not* reuse the post-hit invulnerability window, which would also grant blink immunity). Directed to: Producer — affects feel and the field's effective durability against ramming.
- **Q1 — Which enemies gain a field, and how does it scale with level?** Options: (A) one global level curve for all regular ships; (B) per-archetype data-driven `forceFieldHits` in the enemy CSV/editor plus a level bonus; (C) level-scaled spawn chance with a small fixed field; (D) only heavy archetypes. — **Answer (operator): B — "start with a heavier getting stronger fields".** Source: interactive reply. Per-archetype base values, with heavier/larger archetypes (Tank, Harvester) entitled to stronger fields; the level curve strengthens them further.
- **Q2 — Does the field replace or stack on existing health?** Options: (A) separate layer — field absorbs N hits first, then normal `EnemyConfig.health` (Harvester keeps 5 HP); (B) the field replaces durability — one hit after break, even the Harvester; (C) merge field + health into a single bubble/total. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. Field is an additive layer in front of existing data-driven health.
- **Q3 — How much feedback and balance evidence?** Options: (A) full — shared bubble (distinct from player's), absorb flash, break flash/cue, gym control to force fields, level-gym parity, bot-batch evidence at L1/L5/L10; (B) bubble + flash only, no audio, no bot batch; (C) minimal body tint instead of a bubble. — **Answer (operator): A.** Source: interactive reply. Full feedback surface and balance evidence.
- **Q4 — Should heavy archetypes show a field at level 1, or only from a start level?** Options: (A) fields appear only from a start depth (level-1 run untouched), with the level curve adding field hits past level 2; (B) heavy archetypes show base field hits from level 1. — **Answer (operator): "This needs to be tunable on a per enemy basis, so some will have shields from level 2, others level 3 or more."** Source: interactive reply. Per-archetype `forceFieldStartLevel`; no field at level 1 for any archetype by default; some archetypes start at level 2, others later.
- **Q5 — Confirm the concrete level curve (L1–2: 0, L3–4: +1, L5–6: +2, L7–8: +3, L9–10: +4, base per archetype, cap 5).** Options: (A) adopt table; (B) bases all 0; (C) different shape. — **Answer (operator): "See 1 (use subtle variations of this curve for different enemies)."** Source: interactive reply. Adopted a three-field linear model — `forceFieldStartLevel`, `forceFieldStartHits`, `forceFieldMaxHits` (at level 10), `clamp(round(lerp), 0, 5)` — giving each archetype a subtle per-enemy variation of the reference curve.
- **Open item carried to review (assumption, not yet confirmed):** enemy fields absorb only player **bullet** damage; player contact/ram behaviour is unchanged (both destroyed, AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT). If shields should absorb rams too, that is a product change to confirm during brief review.
## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-24 — Planned (plan skill).** Decomposed into 7 children
  (test-first ordering, wired via `wl dep`):
  - Resolver and codec contract tests (AH-0MVM8GQKI006B50M) — AC1 (red)
  - Force-field config and resolver (AH-0MVM8GRQ8006HGPK) — AC1
  - Entity field and ram contract tests (AH-0MVM8GTG7002IRTL) — AC2 (red)
  - Entity force-field layer (AH-0MVM8GUZG008AWSU) — AC2
  - Shared force-field bubble feedback (AH-0MVM8GW7W004SI0E) — AC3
  - Game and gym spawn parity (AH-0MVM8GXEF009883O) — AC4
  - Docs, tuning table, bot-batch evidence (AH-0MVM8GYPM002Z3PR) — AC5
- **2026-10-24 — AC2 rewritten** per plan Q&A Q6 = **B**: a shielded enemy's
  field absorbs a player ram (one field hit, both sides survive); unshielded
  contact keeps the both-destroyed rule (AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT). Appendix Q6 and
  the OPEN QUESTION Q6a (ram re-arm duration) added.
- **2026-10-24 — Effort/risk re-estimated:** Medium / High (13/25),
  expected 28.8 h, confidence 87% — see effort_and_risk_skill comment.
- **2026-10-24 — Covered:** tree-coverage review `proceed` (100%), parent ACs
  1–5 traced to children.

data.description:
# Intake brief — What does Field of Thorns do? (AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T)

## Headline

The Thorn Field power-up (reported as "Field of Thorns") is fully wired but
invisible: it grants 2–6 free rams with no in-world feedback, and a hold-full
grant is spent after those rams once. Give it an obvious, visible presence —
a shared lime spiked aura around the ship, a distinct absorb burst when a ram
is used, and a recharge so the field keeps doing something all run.

## Problem statement

The Thorn Field upgrade appears to do nothing. The mechanics are wired
(AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z): while armed, ramming an enemy destroys it without
costing a life, for a level-resolved budget of 2–6 rams. But there is no
in-world visual (no aura, no absorb feedback — only a small HUD row), and a
hold-full (permanent) grant gives a one-off budget that is inert once spent,
so the upgrade reads as dead weight.

## Users

- **Players** collecting Thorn Field drops and taking the hold-full "Thorn
  Field" permanent upgrade.

**User story:** "As a player, when I pick up the Thorn Field or take it as a
hold-full upgrade, I can see it has armed my ship, I can see each ram I absorb
work, and the field keeps re-arming so the upgrade stays meaningful."

## Acceptance Criteria

Measurable, testable.

- **Visible aura.** While the Thorn Field is armed (active with ≥ 1 ram
   charge), a lime spiked aura radiates from the ship in **PlayScene and every
   combat/power-up gym** (`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymFormationScene`),
   drawn through one shared helper in `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts`
   (gym↔game parity). The aura reflects the remaining charge count (e.g.
   rotating spike count and/or intensity) and clears when the budget is spent
   or the window expires.
- **Absorb feedback.** When a ram is absorbed (`tryConsumeThornsRam()` →
   true in the shared ram branch), the enemy is destroyed as today **and** a
   distinct lime spike-shatter burst + cue fires at the collision, visibly
   different from a normal player hit. No absorb when the field is exhausted
   or inactive (rams hurt normally again).
- **Recharge (Q2=c).** The field regains one ram charge automatically on a
   level-resolved interval while active: a permanent (hold-full) field
   recharges for the whole run; a field-pickup window recharges while its
   window is still active, up to the level-resolved max budget. New
   `thornsRecharge` axis in `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` (draft values — see
   assumptions).
- **HUD.** The existing `Thorn Field xN` row keeps showing remaining
   charges; for an armed field it also shows the recharge countdown (next ram
   in Ns). A permanent (hold-full) field that is mid-recharge at 0 charges
   also shows the countdown, so the row is never an inert bare label. Stacks
   and remaining values continue straight from the shared registry.
- **Documentation.** The GDD power-up table (§4.4.3, `docs/Game Design
   Document.md` row 920) gains the Thorn recharge axis; code comments and any
   related docs/README notes are updated.
- **Tests & parity.** Unit tests for the recharge clock and aura helper,
   regression tests for absorb feedback (game + gyms), the existing parity
   sweeps (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`,
   `choicePool.parity.test.ts` and the equivalence/duplicate-body guard) stay
   green, and the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **gym↔game parity:** all visual and recharge behaviour lives once in the
  shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, shared `EffectsRegistry`) and is consumed
  by both the game and every gym — no divergent copies (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **Mechanics scope:** the only mechanics change is the recharge (Q2=c).
  Ramming stays destroy-enemy-no-score; exhaust/expiry behaviour is unchanged.
- Visual-only for the aura (Q1=a): no passive contact damage.
- UK English; escape only backticks; no changes to `.pi/`, `skill/`,
  `command/` directories.
- Deterministic visuals (pure functions of registry state, frame-rate
  independent) so game, gyms and tests agree.

## Existing state

- `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.thorns` = "Thorn Field" (`src/powerups/types.ts:251`),
  full level specs (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts:854-883`, thornsAbsorbs
  2→6, thornsDuration 8→16 s).
- Registry: `_thornsRemaining`, `thornsRemaining()`, `hasThornsRam()`,
  `tryConsumeThornsRam()`, expiry clears the budget
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts:391-397, 1060-1090`).
- Shared ram branch consumes the field (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:1286-1298`).
- HUD row + stacks (`src/ui/HUD.ts:499-533`).
- No in-world visual exists for thorns; the shared visual seam is
  `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` (shield bubble, force-field
  bubble, phase ghost), called from `PlayScene`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`,
  `GymFormationScene`.

## Desired change

1. Add shared `drawThornsAura(graphics, player, registry)` + constants to
   `CombatEffectVisuals.ts` (neon-lime `ICON_COLORS.thorns` 0x99ff33 family,
   spiked halo echoing `drawThorns` in `src/powerups/icons.ts:562-583`).
2. Each of the three scenes owns a thorns graphics object, draws the aura in
   `_updateVisuals`/`_updateEffectVisuals` and clears it (mirrors the
   force-field bubble wiring).
3. Absorb feedback: the shared ram branch, when `tryConsumeThornsRam()`
   returns true, triggers a shared "thorn absorb" VFX/sound seam (spike
   shatter burst at the collision, distinct from `_hitPlayer` cue).
4. Recharge: new `thornsRecharge` level axis + registry recharge clock
   advanced in the shared `EffectsRegistry.tick`, refilling the budget one
   ram at a time (permanent grants: whole run; timed windows: while the
   window is active), capped at the level-resolved max.
5. HUD: recharge countdown for an armed field.
6. GDD row update; regression + parity tests.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — add recharge clock state, level-resolved
  `thornsRecharge` interval, advance in `tick()`, refill in
  `tryConsumeThornsRam` path; keep existing accessors.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — add `thornsRecharge` axis to the `thorns`
  spec and the typed variable set (~line 1080).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.ts` — new shared `drawThornsAura`
  helper + constants (aura visual, spent/expiry clearing).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shared ram branch: absorb feedback seam
  (burst/cue) when the field absorbs.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — thorns graphics object +
  `drawThornsAura` in the per-frame visuals; absorb burst spawn.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — recharge countdown for an armed field.
- Tests: `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`,
  parity sweeps (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/powerUpLeveling.parity.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/choicePool.parity.test.ts`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Thorn Field row (line 920) gains the
  recharge axis.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** (Some power-ups appear to do nothing, completed,
  v0.1.14) — wired the thorn rams into the shared combat core. This item is
  the visibility + recharge gap on top of it; partial overlap, rewritten to
  address only the differences (see Appendix Q1/Q2).
- **AH-0MVCRC1Q0007JAV1** (5 net-new power-ups, completed) — catalogue,
  level curves and registry for thorns.
- **AH-0MV1BIX1W006XF95** (force field reflector, completed) — the shared
  force-field bubble precedent for a per-scene graphics + shared draw helper.
- **AH-0MUAYB5HR001HDYC** (shield bubble ending fade) — shared visual
  continuity precedent; the aura should mirror its pure-function-of-state
  style.
- **AH-0MVI4KTD8000FBJ7** (power-ups in hull-full screen, completed) — thorns
  is in the hold-full pool; the permanent grant is what this item makes
  visible/useful.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (recharge values):** draft `thornsRecharge` axis — 12 s base →
  5 s cap, `linear-clamped`, k = -1, discrete (patterned on `strikeInterval`).
  Values are a starting point for implementer/balance review, not gospel.
- **Assumption (recharge scope):** recharge runs only while the field is
  armed (active). A spent one-off pickup window recharges within its window;
  a permanent grant recharges across the whole run. The clock stops when the
  window ends.
- **Assumption (visual semantics):** spike count/intensity maps to remaining
  charge count so the spent state is readable; exact proportions are
  implementer choice within the shared helper.
- **Risk:** scope creep toward a passive-contact-damage "field" — rejected
  (Q1=a); record as a separate item if wanted.
- **Risk:** aura confusion with Shield/Force Field bubbles — mitigate with
  the thorns lime colour + spike motif that already exist in the icon.
- **Risk:** parity drift if scenes hand-roll the aura — mitigated by the
  single shared helper and existing duplicate-body guards.
- **Risk:** recharge making Thorn Field too strong — cap the budget at the
  level-resolved max and floor the interval at 5 s.
- **Risk:** recharge regressing existing permanent-grant tests
  (`PlayScene.test.ts:7118`, `mineralLayer.test.ts:289`) — the recharge is
  additive on top of `applyCollect('thorns', true) → hasThornsRam()`, so the
  grant itself and the first absorptions must behave exactly as today.

## Related work (automated report — find-related)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** – Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed)
- **AH-0MVI4KTD8000FBJ7** – Not all power-ups are appearing in the hull-full screen (completed)
- **AH-0MUTPEHYW005YP3C** – Test: P10 timed field pickup and permanent stacking effects (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: appears, effect, field, needs, nothing, upgrade, visible
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: appears, effect, field, needs, nothing, upgrade, visible
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md` — matched: appears, effect, field, needs, nothing, upgrade, visible

> Full report persisted at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T.md`.

## Plan review notes (implementation guidance)

Recorded by the `plan` skill's automated review of this brief. These are
guidance additions only — goal, scope and acceptance criteria intent are
unchanged.

- **Reuse the existing recharge engine seam (reuse check).**
  `EffectsRegistry.tick(dt)` already forwards `dt` to
  `PowerUpLevelStore.tickRecharge(dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts:705`,
  AH-0MV82I8IL0012RXY AC1/AC5), which is the shared per-charge recharge clock
  the game and every gym advance identically. Two axis conventions already
  exist for recharge:
  - rate style — `phaseRechargeRate` / `teleportRechargeRate`, unit `/s`,
    `exponential-saturation` (the recharge axes' dominant convention, kept
    monotonic non-decreasing in charges/second);
  - interval style — `strikeInterval`, unit `s`, `linear-clamped`, `k = -1`
    (the draft `thornsRecharge` values in this brief).

  Whichever convention is chosen, the derived rate (`1 / interval`) must stay
  monotonic non-decreasing across levels (the invariant every existing
  interval axis documents), and the recharge clock must advance only on the
  shared `tick` path — never per-scene. Reusing the store's clock is preferred
  over a second parallel timer.
- **Test-first ordering.** Write the recharge-clock tests
  (`src/powerups/effects.test.ts`), the aura-helper tests
  (`src/scenes/core/CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts`) and the absorb-feedback
  regression tests (game + gyms) before wiring the scenes, so AC1–AC3 are
  observable before the visuals land.
- **No phasing decision.** This item is a single vertical slice (~22 h
  recommended effort, Low risk); it is small enough that splitting into
  sub-phases would add overhead without reducing risk. It is therefore planned
  as one slice with no child items: tests, shared core, scenes, HUD, docs and
  parity sweeps in one change.
- **Aura/absorb determinism.** Both helpers must be pure functions of registry
  state plus the frame clock handed in by the caller (mirroring the
  shield-bubble fade in AH-0MUAYB5HR001HDYC), so game, gyms and unit tests
  agree frame for frame.
- **Estimate currency.** The effort/risk report already on this item
  (Small effort, Low risk, 2026-10-24) predates only these guidance notes —
  scope is unchanged, so no re-estimate was run.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should 'obvious and visible' mean?" — Answer (operator): **A —
  Visual-only**: lime spiked aura around the ship while armed, burst/flash +
  cue when a ram is absorbed; mechanics otherwise unchanged. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q: "The permanent Thorn Field currently spends its 2 rams once and is inert
  for the rest of the run — in scope?" — Answer (operator): **C — recharge
  one ram on a timer** (level-resolved interval; see assumptions for draft
  values). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Where must the effect apply?" — Answer (operator): **A — game and all
  gyms through the shared `CombatEffectVisuals` helper (parity)**. Source:
  interactive reply.

  154b7adb); no in-world visual exists today (only the HUD row,

## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: with the dev JSONL sink moving to an in-memory per-run buffer (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3), a page reload or crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail. Streaming telemetry batches to the dev server during the run — instead of one run-end upload — bounds that loss to at most one flushed batch (~64 records, ~1.3 s of play) and removes the page-reload regression that localStorage previously masked.

## Context

- Parent/related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3 (in-memory dev sink; this item is explicitly deferred there).
- Current flow: the JsonlTelemetrySink buffers records in memory, flushes batches of 64 to the sink, and the whole run is POSTed once at run end (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash before that POST loses the entire run's telemetry; a reload also loses the buffer entirely once it is no longer localStorage-backed.
- Dev only: the same reasoning applies to the production remote sink, which already streams batches via `HttpTelemetryTransport` (with retry/backoff), so production is not affected.

## Proposed design

- Send each flushed batch to the dev endpoint as it is produced (`POST /api/telemetry/upload`) instead of (or in addition to) the run-end upload.
- The server (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) currently stores each upload as one complete `session-<stamp>.jsonl` and runs the automatic evaluation per upload; a per-batch POST would create many tiny recordings and repeated evaluations. The endpoint (or a new `part` protocol) must therefore either:
  - append JSONL records to the run's open session file keyed by a run id/seed, and evaluate once at run end, or
  - keep the run-end upload and add a lightweight "heartbeat/checkpoint" mechanism that only recovers the tail on demand.
- UX/offline: batches sent while the dev server is unreachable should stay in the memory buffer (or a bounded queue) and be retried at run end; at most one batch may be lost on a hard crash.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A mid-run crash/reload followed by a run-end state loses no more than one flushed batch (~64 records / ~1.3 s) of telemetry; the rest is recoverable from the dev server.
- AC2: The server session file for a run contains its records exactly once (no duplication from partial + final uploads), and the automatic evaluation still runs once per run.
- AC3: Dev CLI tooling (`record-session`, `capture-gameplay`, `verify-dev-telemetry`) continues to work unchanged in behaviour.
- AC4: Full project test suite passes.

## Status

Open decision item — parked until the in-memory sink (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) lands. Do not implement concurrently with that item in the same worktree.
data.title: Crash resilience: incremental telemetry upload so a mid-run reload loses at most one batch

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

# Intake brief — Full-suite runs dirty the main checkout ship-config.csv

> **Source request (verbatim):** "Full-suite test runs (observed with
> changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leave
> src/data/ship-config.csv modified in the MAIN checkout
> (thrustAcceleration/maxSpeed/frictionDeceleration/controlScheme changes),
> even though the suite runs from a worktree. A test exercising
> GymPlayer.saveShipConfig writes through the dev-server CSV plugin whose root
> resolves to the main checkout (likely via the symlinked node_modules / vite
> project root). This trips the implement dirty-tree gate on later sessions,
> requiring a git checkout restore; it can also silently clobber an operator's
> tuned ship config. … add a guard so suites never write the repo's tracked
> CSV."

## Headline

Full-suite test runs leak writes to the tracked `src/data/ship-config.csv` in the **main checkout** even when the suite runs from a worktree, breaking the implement dirty-tree gate and risking silent clobbering of an operator-tuned ship config. Fix the dev-server CSV plugin's root resolution and add a guard so suites never write a tracked repository CSV.

## Problem statement

Running the full test suite (observed during changed-scope validation at a worktree on AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) leaves `src/data/ship-config.csv` modified in the MAIN checkout — `thrustAcceleration`/`maxSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration`/`controlScheme` diverge from the committed values — despite the suite having run from a worktree. The only writer of the tracked CSVs is the dev-server CSV plugin (`vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`): its write handler resolves `resolve(root, 'src/data/ship-config.csv')` where `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274), and the config store's dev-mode save (`saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves`, gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV`, which is `true` under vitest) issues a **relative** `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (`src/core/configStore.ts` lines 397–405, 569–586). In vitest's happy-dom integration project (default `window.location` = `http://localhost:3000`, verified in the installed vitest source), happy-dom's fetch resolves relative URLs against that origin — so a real (un-mocked) save PUTs to `http://localhost:3000/api/csv/...`; whatever server answers there can write through a root that points at the main checkout. Worktrees symlink `node_modules` to the main checkout (confirmed on four live worktrees), which lets Vite's project-root/package-root inference escape to the main checkout. The worktree's own `csv-seed.test.ts` reads its CSVs via `__dirname`, so a leaked write to the *other* checkout is not caught by the seed tests in the active checkout. Consequences: the implement dirty-tree gate fails on later sessions (manual `git checkout` restore required), and an operator-tuned ship config can be silently clobbered; it likely also explains intermittent `csv-seed` / `<suite exited 1>` smoke failures (AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL, AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP, AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2).

## Users

- **Developers / AI agents running the suite** — "As a developer I want suite runs to never modify tracked config files in any checkout, so the implement dirty-tree gate stays green and I don't have to restore files manually."
- **Designers/operators tuning ship config** — "As a designer I want my tuned `ship-config.csv` to survive test runs, so my balance work isn't silently overwritten."
- **Test suite maintainers** — "As a test author I want tests to exercise save behaviour against isolated fixtures, so the suite is deterministic and hermetic."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No tracked-file writes from suites** — Running the audit-accepted full suite (`npm --silent test`: `unit` + `integration` projects) from a worktree leaves every tracked `src/data/*.csv` (`ship-config.csv`, `enemy-configs.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`) unchanged in **both** the active worktree and the main checkout. Verified by an automated pre/post `git status --porcelain` of both checkouts that runs as part of the change's tests (a regression guard the suite itself asserts).
2. **Root isolation in the plugin** — The CSV plugin never resolves write targets to a checkout other than the active project root: the implicit `process.cwd()` default is replaced by an explicit, verified root (derived from the Vite-resolved root, or an explicit option), and any request whose resolved target escapes the active root is refused with no file I/O (HTTP error + logged reason). Existing explicit-root test fixtures keep working unchanged.
3. **Test-mode write guard in the store** — Under the vitest/test harness (`import.meta.env.MODE === 'test'` detected in `configStore.ts`), `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` must never write a tracked repository file: they either update the registry only (documented no-op wrt disk, preserving registry semantics used by tests) or route writes to an isolated temp fixture. A direct unit test covers each save function under test mode asserting no file on disk changes.
4. **Escape route closed** — No test can PUT through a live dev-server endpoint by accident: relative `/api/csv/...` fetches in the happy-dom project must resolve against a test-controlled origin (explicit bridge/stub), never a stray `localhost` server that could answer from the main checkout. Add a comment in the integration tests documenting the relative-fetch/bridge pattern and verifying the bridge is installed for every real save.
5. **Documentation and full suite** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (plugin root semantics, test-mode guard and store save behaviour) and any relevant wiki/docs entries. The full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and the existing seed/validation tests (`csv-seed.test.ts`, `configStore.*`, plugin tests, gym save tests) remain green.

## Constraints

- Dev-only behaviour is preserved: while `npm run dev` runs from the active checkout, gym Save/Save As must still persist through the plugin to the committed CSVs (read-write dev workflow, AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA). Production builds stay read-only (`apply: 'serve'`).
- Atomic-write semantics (temp file + rename) and the post-save registry re-read (`reReadRegistry`) must be preserved on the success path.
- Test isolation is a requirement, not an option: current unit/integration tests already pin temp fixtures via explicit `root`; the gap is the default path and the dev-mode relative fetch. Do not weaken existing fixture patterns.
- Worktree isolation rules apply: implementation happens in a worktree; the main checkout is never edited directly.
- UK English for prose/comments; Markdown for work-item and code-doc prose.

## Existing state

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — `configCsvPlugin(options)`: `const root = options.root ?? process.cwd();` (line 274); `handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath), …)` for ship/enemy/difficulty CSVs. Registered in `vite.config.ts` with no options (`configCsvPlugin()`, so default root = `process.cwd()` of the dev server / test process).
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `isDev()` = `import.meta.env.DEV === true` (line 97); `fetchCsv`/`putCsv` use relative `/api/csv/...` URLs (lines 397–405, 569–586); `saveShipConfig`/`saveEnemyConfig`/`saveDifficultyCurves` (lines ~612–660) gate only on `isDev()`.
- Vitest config (`vitest.config.ts`) — `unit` (node) and `integration` (happy-dom, default origin `http://localhost:3000`) projects; `isolate: true`; the full suite is `unit` + `integration`.
- `src/core/configStore.integration.test.ts` (lines 80, 121–133) and `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — real plugin behind an ephemeral HTTP server against a **temp** root with an explicit fetch bridge; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts` / `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — `vi.mock('../../core/configStore')` replacing `saveShipConfig` with an in-process registry seed; safe pattern to keep.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — reads CSVs via `__dirname`, i.e. relative to the **active** checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it.
- Worktree layout — `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with `node_modules` symlinked to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed on four live worktrees: wl-AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40-*, wl-AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V-*, wl-AH-0MVAUU594007S92Q-*, wl-AH-0MVNT27XR0080I3C-*).

## Desired change

1. Make the plugin's write root explicit and safe: derive it from the Vite server's resolved project root (with an explicit override option), and refuse any write whose target resolves outside the active root. This removes the unpredictable `process.cwd()` default.
2. Add a store-level test-mode guard so the vitest harness can never write tracked files (registry-only no-op or temp-fixture routing), closing the relative-fetch escape route at the source.
3. Harden regression coverage: a suite-run cleanliness assertion (pre/post `git status` on both checkouts) plus unit tests for the new root guard and the test-mode guard.
4. Document the safe patterns (explicit roots, fetch bridges, module mocks) alongside the plugin and store modules.

## Key Files

- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — replace the `process.cwd()` default root with an explicit/Vite-resolved root that is verified against the active checkout; add the escape-refusal guard; update `ConfigCsvPluginOptions` docs.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.test.ts` — tests for default-root behaviour (must not write outside active root) and the escape-refusal guard.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — add test-mode detection to `isDev()`/save guards; document relative-fetch + bridge pattern.
- `src/core/configStore.test.ts` / `configStore.integration.test.ts` — tests for test-mode save no-op/temp routing; fixture pattern comments.
- `vite.config.ts` — pass an explicit root derived from `server.config.root` if the plugin cannot self-derive it.
- `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` — optionally extend the seed check to also assert a clean worktree/main-checkout diff (the suite-run cleanliness guard may live here or in a new small test).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` (only if behaviour changes; otherwise untouched) — `_onSave` consumes `saveShipConfig`'s `ok/reason`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole": where the leak was first observed (`discovered-from`).
- **AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL** — "[test-failure] csv-seed.test.ts / configStore.integration.test.ts — ship-config.csv diverges from DEFAULT_CONFIG": the smoke symptom of a leaked write (`thrustAcceleration 390` vs `300`).
- **AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT** — "enemy-configs.csv working-tree change removes header and trailing newline (fails csv-seed tests)": sibling symptom on the enemy CSV.
- **AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP**, **AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2** — "[test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test": possibly same intermittent root cause.
- **AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA** (config-store epic), **AH-0MUE2MHRC0090AXP** (CSV plugin), **AH-0MUE2MIK9001TK88** (integration tests) — origin of the dev write-back design being hardened here.
- **AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V** — "Ship config controlScheme does not survive game server restart": dev-server persistence semantics for ship config.
- **AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4** — "Gym config save strips the CSV comment header block": another save-path quirk.
- **AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM** (open) — "Dev-mode write-back: gym Save to repo persists bot tuning": the same "dev writes to tracked repo data" family; keep separate.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-broad guard breaks the legit dev save flow** — mitigation: scope the refusal to (a) targets outside the active root and (b) test-mode; the dev-mode save path from the active checkout must keep working (AC2 keeps explicit-root fixtures valid).
- **Stray server on the happy-dom origin (localhost:3000) still receives writes if only the plugin changes** — the store-level test-mode guard (AC3) is the belt-and-braces fix; do not rely on the plugin alone.
- **Root-cause mechanism partially inferred** — the exact process that answers the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run was not reproduced deterministically in this intake; the implementer must reproduce and confirm before finalising the guard wording (record the reproduction in the work item). Non-blocking for the fix: ACs are observable-outcome based.
- **Scope creep** — protecting against an operator's accidental save overwriting a tuned config in the *browser/UI* (e.g. a confirmation prompt) is a separate UX concern; record it as a separate item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption** — `npm --silent test` remains the audit-accepted full suite; suite runs from implement worktrees use symlinked node_modules; vitest happy-dom default origin is `http://localhost:3000` and happy-dom resolves relative fetches against it (verified in installed `vitest`/`happy-dom` sources at intake time).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed context (title + description of AH-0MVKYQWSW0067F12) already contained the observed symptom, the primary hypothesis (root resolution via symlinked node_modules / vite project root), and the suggested fix directions. Research performed during intake:

- **Q (self): "Which code path is the only writer of the tracked CSVs?"** — Answer (Map): `configCsvPlugin.handlePut` → `atomicWrite(resolve(root, relPath))` in `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`; `root` defaults to `process.cwd()` (line 274). Source: code inspection of `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`, `vite.config.ts` (plugin registered without options).
- **Q (self): "How does a suite-run write escape the temp-fixture pattern?"** — Answer (Map): all plugin instantiations in tests pass explicit temp roots (`configCsvPlugin.test.ts` line 100/447, `configStore.integration.test.ts` line 80) and GymPlayer tests mock the store — so the leak is not from these; the store's dev-mode save issues a relative `fetch('/api/csv/...')` (configStore.ts lines 397–405, 569–586) gated only on `import.meta.env.DEV` (true under vitest). In the happy-dom integration project, happy-dom's `Fetch` resolves the relative URL against `window.location.href` (verified in `node_modules/happy-dom/lib/fetch/Fetch.js`), whose vitest default is `http://localhost:3000` (verified in `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DC7d2Pf8.js` line 343). A real server on that origin with a root at the main checkout receives the PUT.
- **Q (self): "Why does the worktree's root resolve to the main checkout?"** — Answer (Map): worktree `node_modules` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules` (confirmed via `ls -la` on four live worktrees), so Vite's package-root/workspace-root detection and any module-relative path resolution can escape to the main checkout. Likely, not yet reproduced end-to-end (recorded in Risks).
- **Q (self): "Why doesn't the active checkout's csv-seed test catch the leak?"** — Answer (Map): `src/data/csv-seed.test.ts` reads CSVs via `resolve(__dirname, …)`, i.e. the active checkout only; a write leaked to the other checkout is invisible to it. Source: code inspection.
- **Q (self): "Are there existing related items?"** — Answer (Map): yes — AH-0MUKQB2MX000PSLL (ship-config smoke failure), AH-0MUL0WS9P006NUCT (enemy-config analogue), AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP / AH-0MV6MK7BJ002V9H2 (generic suite-exit-1), AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V, AH-0MUF6NJ83003Y1J4, AH-0MVBJ0DUI009B6AM. Source: `wl search` during intake step 2.
- **Open question for the implementer (not a producer blocker):** reproduce the exact answering server/process on the happy-dom origin during a worktree suite run and record it; the ACs are outcome-verifiable regardless.

# Intake brief: Upgrade text must reflect the actual upgrade for each weapon and level

## Problem statement

When the player is offered an upgrade, the on-screen text does not say what that
specific weapon or power-up actually gains at that level: every option shows the
same base-item description (identical for every weapon **and** every level), so
the choice is a blind guess. The secondary issue: even where a level-delta
summary is shown (hold-full choice), it is generated from shared curves with no
per-weapon filtering, so non-AoE weapons falsely report a "+N% AoE radius".

## Users

As a **player**, when I defeat a mini-boss and am offered an upgrade, or when I
fill my hold and choose a level-up, I want the option text to tell me what that
weapon/power-up gains at that specific next level — e.g. `+1 Projectiles, +17%
Fire rate` — and to never promise an effect the item does not have (e.g. AoE on
a non-AoE weapon).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 — Mini-boss reward upgrade options carry a level-accurate change summary
  (`changeSummary`) showing the real delta between the current level and the
  offered level (e.g. `+1 Projectiles, +17% Fire rate`), matching the deltas the
  hold-full choice already shows. Applies to every offered `weapon-level` and
  `power-up-level` option from `buildUpgradeOptions` (src/powerups/unlocks.ts),
  for weapons via `summariseWeaponLevelChange` and power-ups via
  `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`.
- AC2 — The change summary only lists variables that **actually change the game
  behaviour of that weapon/power-up** at that level: implemented (MVP) variables
  only; no unimplemented/planned variables; no `aoeRadius` delta on weapons
  without an `aoe` descriptor. Verified with a regression test that a non-AoE
  weapon never yields an "AoE" fragment.
- AC3 — The same option model is shared: both the mini-boss reward and the
  hold-full choice build level-up options through one code path (no divergent
  copies), so the text cannot drift between the game and the gyms
  (gym↔game parity — no gym shows mini-boss rewards, but `GymWeaponLeveling`
  consumes the shared hold-full candidates). The existing hold-full behaviour
  (level-accurate summary + `★ New` badge) must not regress.
- AC4 — Testing/validation: new unit tests cover (i) a weapon-level reward
  option carries a non-empty, level-accurate summary; (ii) a power-up-level
  reward option carries its summary; (iii) non-AoE weapons never report an AoE
  delta; (iv) summary text differs between levels where the maths differ. Full
  project test suite must pass.
- AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (no
  catalogue changes are anticipated; the docs guards in `weaponLevelingDocs.test.ts`
  must still pass).

## Constraints

- Do not change upgrade maths, curves, caps, or the MVP variable set — display
  copy only.
- Do not surface 'planned'/unimplemented upgrade variables (damage, pierce,
  bounce, homing, chainCount, splitCount, critChance, statusChance,
  bulletSpeed, bulletLifetime, spreadAngle) in player-facing text.
- Keep deltas computed from the shared level maths (single source of truth —
  `summariseWeaponLevelChange` / `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`) — never
  hard-code numbers.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `buildChoiceCandidates` populates `changeSummary`
  for hold-full `weapon-level` / `power-up-level` offers (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR).
- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — `buildUpgradeOptions` (mini-boss reward,
  AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH) reuses `toChoiceOption` and **omits `changeSummary`**, so
  the overlay shows only the base catalogue description for every weapon/level.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `summariseWeaponLevelChange` iterates the 4 MVP
  variables (`fireRate`, `projectileCount`, `bulletSize`, `aoeRadius`) with no
  per-weapon applicability filter; `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` curves are shared by
  all weapons, so text is near-identical across weapons at the same level.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — renders the option name, description line
  and detail line (`'★ New'` or `changeSummary`); a missing `changeSummary`
  renders no detail line at all.
- Gyms: `GymWeaponLeveling`/`GymPowerUpLeveling` consume the shared hold-full
  candidates, so they inherit any fix automatically.

## Desired change

1. Populate `changeSummary` in `buildUpgradeOptions` for every owned
   `weapon-level`/`power-up-level` offer, using the same shared summarisers and
   the offered level (`level → level + 1`).
2. Extract a single "build level-up option" helper used by both
   `buildChoiceCandidates` and `buildUpgradeOptions` (parity AC3), or
   minimally have `buildUpgradeOptions` reuse the existing candidate builder.
3. Add per-weapon applicability filtering to the weapon change summary: skip
   `aoeRadius` when the weapon has no `aoe` descriptor (checked once per
   weapon); keep the implemented MVP variable set otherwise.
4. Add regression tests (`unlocks.test.ts`, `weaponLevels.test.ts`, and the
   `choice.test.ts` parity guard) covering the ACs above.

The base catalogue description line (`option.description`) stays as it is — it
tells the player what the item is; the new summary tells them what the level
gains.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` — `buildUpgradeOptions`: add `changeSummary`
  (+ `level` text already present); single source shared with hold-full.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — extract/reuse the level-up option builder so both
  paths stay in parity; `choice.ts` is the canonical builder.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — `summariseWeaponLevelChange`: per-weapon
  applicability filter (no AoE delta on non-AoE weapons).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — no behavioural change expected (it
  already renders `changeSummary`); verify only.
- Tests: `src/powerups/unlocks.test.ts`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.test.ts`,
  `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` (shared-builder parity).

## Related work

- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH — Mini-boss reward: upgrade-or-unlock + locked pool
  (completed; owner of `buildUpgradeOptions`).
- AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR — Show upgrade change summary + New badge in the
  hold-full choice list (completed; introduced `changeSummary` rendering).
- AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD — Upgrade and weapon descriptions (completed; item copy
  from shared catalogues).
- AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J — per-weapon level state (weapon level machinery).
- AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6 — power-up level machine (parent of power-up levels).
- AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG — refactored fire rates as beat subdivisions.

### Automated related-work report (find-related)

Additional related items surfaced by `/skill:find-related`:

- AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV — Feature: Permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling
  (completed; the reward seam that applies these upgrades).
- AH-0MUX9T7QA008CW73 — F4: Choice and HUD consume permanent/effective levels
  (completed; the choice/HUD level consumption seam this copy sits on).
- AH-0MUAYB5UK0052P1D — Symbols for weapons do not reflect what the weapon does
  (completed; direct precedent: display copy had drifted from actual behaviour).
- Repository docs to consult: `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4.2 Weapon
  Leveling), `README.md`.
- Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- Display-only change; no gameplay/balance impact (low risk).
- Assumption: the operator wants only **implemented** (MVP) deltas shown — no
  planned/unimplemented variables (confirmed via Q3).
- Assumption: both surfaces must be fixed (confirmed via Q1, answer "C") with
  data-driven numeric deltas (confirmed via Q2, answer "A").
- Assumption: the base item description line is retained unchanged alongside the
  new level summary.
- Scope risk: authoring per-weapon prose copy or expanding to non-MVP variables
  is deliberately out of scope; if wanted, create a follow-up work item
  (`discovered-from:AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON`).
- Minor risk: tests asserting the old per-weapon summary output (e.g.
  `weaponLevels.test.ts` 'contains a percentage scalar') may need small updates
  if a non-AoE weapon no longer yields an AoE fragment — keep AC-visible maths
  unchanged.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Which upgrade screens must show level-accurate text?**
  (a) Mini-boss reward only, (b) hold-full choice only, (c) both.
  — **Answer (operator): "C"** — both surfaces. Recommended option was (c);
  operator selected (c). Source: interactive reply, intake session 2026-10-23.
  Evidence: `src/powerups/unlocks.ts` (mini-boss) and `src/powerups/choice.ts`
  (hold-full) both build upgrade options.

- **Q2: What should the upgrade text contain?**
  (a) numeric level-deltas from the real level maths (only variables that
  actually change), (b) hand-authored prose per weapon, (c) numbers plus a short
  weapon-specific sentence.
  — **Answer (operator): "A"** — data-driven numeric deltas. Recommended option
  was (a); operator selected (a). Source: interactive reply.
  Evidence: `summariseWeaponLevelChange` / `summarisePowerUpLevelChange` already
  compute exactly this from `resolveWeaponAtLevel` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`.

- **Q3: Should the text include the 12 specified-but-unimplemented upgrade
  variables (damage, pierce, bounce, chain, homing, …)?**
  (a) No — only implemented (MVP) variables, (b) yes — all 16 variables.
  — **Answer (operator): "A"** — implemented variables only. Recommended option
  was (a); operator selected (a). Source: interactive reply.
  Evidence: `MVP_UPGRADE_VARIABLES` = fireRate, projectileCount, bulletSize,
  aoeRadius; the remaining variables are `tier: 'planned'` in
  `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`.

No open questions remain.
