# Camera filter driver with WebGL capability probe

Shared infrastructure for approach C of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU: Phaser 4 camera
filters are **WebGL only**, so every filter-based layer needs one guarded,
teardown-exact entry point.

## Goal

As a developer, I want a single shared module that can apply and clear the
Phase Shift camera-filter layers safely on any renderer, so the game and the
gyms never diverge and a headless/canvas build can never crash or leak.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Capability probe.** `supportsCameraFilters(scene)` returns true only when
  the renderer is WebGL *and* the camera exposes a usable filter list; it never
  throws for a stub, a missing camera, or a renderer without `type`.
- **Activation burst.** `applyPhaseDistortionBurst(...)` adds the pixelate +
  barrel/displacement wobble controllers for the documented duration, driven by
  the exported tunables (no hard-coded numbers).
- **Sustained layer.** `applyPhaseSustainedFilter(...)` adds the gentle
  sustained layer (low-strength glow/bloom or barrel) and returns handles for
  teardown.
- **Exact teardown.** `clearPhaseFilters(...)` removes and destroys only the
  controllers this module added, restoring the camera's pre-existing filter
  list unchanged (verified by a test that pre-adds an unrelated filter and
  asserts it survives).
- **Degradation.** When filters are unsupported every function is a documented
  no-op returning a falsy/"unsupported" result; nothing is allocated.
- **No per-frame allocation.** Steady-state updates mutate existing controller
  properties only.
- **Documented.** Module-level JSDoc explains WebGL-only behaviour, the fallback
  contract and every tunable.
- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge. (enforced by the shared driver)
- WebGL capability probe with graceful fallback: filter layers apply only when supported, otherwise degrading to overlay-only layers without throwing. (enforced by the shared driver)

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.ts` — new.
- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.test.ts` — new (see sibling test item).

# Run-end dev telemetry upload overflows the CDP pipe (single >512 MiB message)

Parent: **AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE**. Discovered from **AH-0MVNT25JI004OVKQ**
(diagnosis with instrumentation).

## Problem

The long-run `npm run capture` crash is **not** caused by the recorder chunk
binding. Diagnostics (AH-0MVNT25JI004OVKQ) recorded the largest CDP message of
two soak runs:

- full-run clip (run ended at 226 s): **62.3 MiB** `Network.requestWillBeSent`
- fixed 420 s clip: **14.7 MB** `Network.requestWillBeSent`
- recorder chunk binding max: **384 KB** (p95 278 KB), steady 1 chunk/s

Every largest message is the **run-end dev telemetry upload**:
`POST /api/telemetry/upload` from `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts`, whose body is the
whole raw per-run telemetry NDJSON. Playwright reports the request body as
`request.postData` inside a single `Network.requestWillBeSent` CDP message, so
the message size equals the telemetry body size and grows with run length and
frame/entity density. Playwright's `PipeTransport._dispatch`
(`playwright-core/lib/server/pipeTransport.js:67`, pinned 1.55.1) does
`Buffer.concat(this._pendingBuffers).toString()` and V8 caps strings at
`0x1fffffe8` (512 MiB) → `ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG`, process death mid-recording.

The reported crash at 407.5 s into the fifth clip (23% of the 1800 s cap, no
`Encoding and probing the clip…` line) is consistent with the run ending there
and its telemetry POST crossing 512 MiB.

The upload is on by default in dev builds (`shareTelemetryDev` defaults to
`true`), so a fresh capture profile always uploads.

## Goal / user story

As the person producing long playthrough captures, I want the run-end telemetry
upload to never be delivered as a single >512 MiB CDP message, so a long run
cannot kill the capture process.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Reproduce the mechanism without a multi-hour run: a hermetic test drives the
   upload path (or the capture's upload policy) with a simulated telemetry
   payload above the CDP message budget and asserts the capture path does not
   emit it as one message (chunked/disabled/capped).
2. During capture, the run-end telemetry upload cannot produce a single CDP
   message above a documented, configurable cap (target ≤ 8 MiB), with the cap
   applied either by streaming/chunking the upload or by suppressing it for
   captured runs.
3. A long capture (> 400 s) completes without a transport overflow, verified
   with `--diagnostics` (largest CDP message reported under the cap) and
   recorded on this item.
4. The capture artefact contract is unchanged: the `.action.jsonl` /
   `.capture.json` sidecars are still produced from the page's in-memory buffer
   (the upload is not the export path), `--json` shape and exit codes unchanged.
5. `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` behaviour for normal dev play is either
   unchanged or the change is documented (the setting still governs uploads);
   no production-bundle impact (`npm run check-bundle` passes).
6. Documentation updated where the capture path is documented
   (`docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, the telemetry docs section that describes
   the upload) and the diagnostics finding referenced.
7. Full project test suite passes (through the test skill).

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — capture session startup: where a capture can
  disable/chunk the dev upload (injected setting/flag) before the game boots.
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` — run-end POST of the whole telemetry buffer.
- `src/telemetry/devMode.ts` — `isDevTelemetryUploadEnabled` gate.
- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — `shareTelemetryDev` default.
- `scripts/capture-diagnostics.mjs` — `--diagnostics` transport tap used for the
  verification (largest CDP message).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — capture behaviour and limits.

## Evidence

Full numbers and reasoning: comment on AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE recorded by
AH-0MVNT25JI004OVKQ. Diagnostics artefact schema: `<stem>.diagnostics.json`
(`chunks.*`, `node.*`, `page.*`, `transport.maxMessageBytes` /
`transport.maxMessageSample`).
## Plan clarifications (plan skill, 2026-10-25)

Pre-check (`plan_helpers.py plan-if-needed`): effort **Extra Small**, risk
**Low** → planning was skipped and the six automated review stages ran against
this description instead. They found no missing requirements and created no
children, but added the repo-derived clarifications below (they change *how*
the ACs must be met, not *what* is required).

### The cap must be client-side (the existing server cap is too late)

`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` already rejects oversized bodies —
`DEFAULT_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is **16 MiB**, and `docs/TELEMETRY.md` documents
"bodies over 16 MiB are rejected with `413`". That bound does not help here:
Playwright captures the body in `request.postData` inside the
`Network.requestWillBeSent` CDP message **when the request is sent**, before any
server response exists, so a >512 MiB body still overflows the pipe even though
the dev server would have rejected it. The cap must therefore be enforced in the
page, before `fetch`, and chosen at or below the existing server bound (AC2's
≤ 8 MiB target is compatible and strictly safer).

### Do not suppress the upload by turning `shareTelemetryDev` off

`resolveEffectiveTelemetryConfig` (`src/telemetry/consent.ts`) derives the
collection decision from `isDevTelemetryCollectionEnabled(env, settings)`, and
upload is a strict subset of collection (`src/telemetry/devMode.ts`). A capture
needs collection **on**: `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` sets
`VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true` and reads the page's in-memory buffer to write the
`.action.jsonl` / `.capture.json` sidecars. So seeding
`shareTelemetryDev: false` for a capture would satisfy AC2 but break AC4. Any
capture-side suppression must gate the **upload only** (or be a client-side size
cap), leaving collection and the in-memory buffer intact.

### Additional key files (found during review)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `flushAndUploadDevTelemetry()` is the single
  run-end call site of the uploader.
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` — `DEFAULT_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES`
  (16 MiB) and the `413` path the client cap must not exceed.
- `src/telemetry/consent.ts` — the collection ↔ upload coupling above.
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.test.ts`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — the
  hermetic tests AC1/AC2 need; no browser or Vite server required.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md` (the "Upload at run end" section and the 16 MiB `413`
  bound) plus `src/telemetry/devModeDocs.test.ts`, the docs grep guard those
  edits must keep green.

### Non-blocking question (OPEN QUESTION)

Preferred mechanism is a **client-side cap-and-skip**: a pre-flight size check in
`uploadDevTelemetry` (injected cap seam, default ≤ 8 MiB) that skips the POST
with one actionable line when the buffer is over the cap. It satisfies AC2
verbatim, leaves normal-length dev runs unchanged, and touches neither the
server contract nor the evaluation queue; the cost is that very long runs no
longer upload telemetry at all (documented under AC5/AC6). Chunked/streaming
upload would preserve the upload but needs a new multi-part server contract plus
evaluation-queue changes. Confirm cap-and-skip is the acceptable trade-off; the
existing ACs permit either.

# Config-defined scene setups for scripted gameplay capture

## Problem statement

Multi-scene capture (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC) records several gym scenes into one WebM, driven by a `scenes.json` list. Today a scene entry can only name a `target` key plus `playMs` / `captureMs` / `label`; the scene's **content** is hard-coded by the scene class. Consequences:

- `GymLevel` always starts the player with spread + dual permanently equipped and plays whatever `LevelDefinition` launched it — but nothing in the capture path can supply one.
- `GymFodderEnemies` needs an `enemyKey` and cannot be started from a key at all.
- Both parameterised scenes are therefore excluded from `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` (`unsupported-target`), and the in-page director's `start(key)` accepts no launch data.
- Formation gyms (`GymBoss`, `GymCentipede`, `GymMiniBoss`, …) have fixed rosters and loadouts, so a showcase cannot show "the player with shield level 2 and the rapid weapon, on level 4 wave 2, fighting these enemies".

The recording machinery already supports everything needed except the data: `scene.start(key, data)` is how gyms are launched everywhere else, `LevelDefinition` / `WaveDefinition` are plain serialisable data, `Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` and `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)` are the shared loadout seams, and seeded RNG (`createSeededRng` / `normaliseSeed`) is already used by `GymBotTuning`.

## User stories

- As the maintainer, I can describe a scene's setup (level, waves, enemies, player weapons and power-ups, RNG seed) inside `scenes.json`, so one config produces exactly the gameplay a video needs.
- As the maintainer, I can re-run the same config and get the same recording, so a clip can be re-cut, compared or regenerated after a balance change.
- As a reviewer, a bad setup is rejected **before** the browser boots with an actionable error, instead of recording a blank or unintended scene.
- As an implementer, setups are applied through the same shared seams the shipped game uses, so gym↔game parity (and the duplicate-body guard) is preserved rather than forked.

## Expected behaviour

A scene entry gains an optional `setup` object. Absent `setup` ⇒ today's behaviour, byte-for-byte unchanged. Present ⇒ validated before boot, normalised with documented defaults, passed through the dev-only director into the target scene's `init`, and applied **during the warm-up (`playMs`) window** so the first captured frame already shows the configured state.

Illustrative shape (final field names fixed by C1):

```json
{
  "scenes": [
    {
      "target": "GymLevel",
      "playMs": 2000,
      "captureMs": 4000,
      "label": "level 4, wave 2, shield 2",
      "setup": {
        "seed": 42,
        "level": {
          "level": 4,
          "name": "The Core",
          "waves": [
            { "groups": [{ "enemyKey": "scout", "formation": "grid", "count": 6 }],
              "shootEnabled": true }
          ]
        },
        "startWave": 2,
        "player": { "weapons": ["spread", "dual", "rapid"] },
        "powerUps": { "shield": 2, "smart_bomb": 1 }
      }
    },
    {
      "target": "GymFodderEnemies",
      "playMs": 1500,
      "captureMs": 2500,
      "setup": { "enemy": "grunt", "player": { "weapons": ["spread"] } }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Setup schema and defaults.** A scene entry accepts an optional `setup` object covering at minimum: a `LevelDefinition`-shaped level (`level`, `name`, `waves[]` with `groups[]` and the existing opt-in flags), a starting wave index, the enemy key(s) that select a formation-gym roster, the player loadout (permanent + timed weapon ids, power-up levels), and a `seed`. Every field has a documented default; an entry without `setup` behaves exactly as today (proved by an unchanged-behaviour test).
- **AC2 — Fail-fast validation.** Invalid setups are rejected with `Scene config error: …` and exit 1 **before** any Vite server or browser boots. New stable error codes cover at least: unknown/invalid field, unknown `enemyKey`, unknown formation kind, unknown weapon id, unknown power-up id, non-positive/out-of-range level or wave index, missing required setup for a parameterised target, and a setup supplied to a target that cannot accept it. Codes are asserted in tests rather than on message wording, mirroring the existing `SCENE_CONFIG_ERROR_CODES` pattern.
- **AC3 — Director passes setup through.** The dev-only in-page director exposes `start(key, setup?)` and forwards the setup as `scene.start(key, setup)`, keeping one page and one continuously running `MediaRecorder` (no navigation or reload). `GymLevel` and `GymFodderEnemies` become recordable **when** the setup supplies their required parameter, and remain rejected with a clear `unsupported-target`-class error when it does not. Validation stays shared between CLI and director (single source of truth), and the registry pinning test is updated so the watchable set and the gym files on disk cannot drift.
- **AC4 — Shared setup application, no forked gameplay.** One shared, unit-tested helper applies a normalised setup to a scene's existing seams (`LevelDefinition` hand-off, `Player.equipWeapon`, `PowerUpLevelStore.collect`) inside `init`/`create` before the first captured frame. **No scene-class generation and no duplicated gameplay bodies** — the gym↔game parity convention (AGENTS.md; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard) stays green, and the helper is the only place that knows how a setup becomes play state.
- **AC5 — Determinism.** Setup-driven randomness (enemy/formation placement, drop cadence, any generated content) is seeded from the config, so the same config yields the same scene content run to run; the resolved seed is reported in the `--json` payload. A test asserts identical derived state for two runs of the same seed and different state for different seeds.
- **AC6 — Machine-readable reporting.** The `--json` payload reports, per scene, the **normalised** setup actually applied (defaults filled in) alongside the existing `target` / `playMs` / `captureMs` / `startMs` / `endMs`, so a consumer can reproduce the recording without re-deriving defaults.
- **AC7 — Documentation, examples and gates.** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents the `setup` schema, defaults, error codes and a worked example; `README.md` and `examples/scenes.json` are updated with a setup-bearing example. Hermetic tests cover schema validation, defaults, normalisation, determinism and director pass-through; the full project suite (`/skill:test`), `npm run build` and `npm run check-bundle` all pass.

## Constraints

- **No scene-code generation.** "Scene generator" means a *parametriser* producing launch data for existing shared scenes. Emitting bespoke scene classes would fork the gameplay path and violate the gym↔game parity rule.
- **Dev-only and bundle-inert.** Director and `src/` plumbing stay behind `import.meta.env.DEV`; `npm run check-bundle` must stay green.
- **One recorder, one page.** Scene switching stays in-page; no navigation or reload.
- **WebM only.** No transcoding (no VP9 ffmpeg available).
- **Backward compatible.** Every existing `scenes.json` (including `examples/scenes.json`) keeps working untouched.

## Out of scope

- Generated shipped-game `PlayScene` levels (the "Option C" target) — tracked by AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX, which this epic unblocks by supplying the setup pass-through.
- Runtime (in-UI) editing of scene setups; setups are file-defined only.
- Any change to the shipped game's balance, catalogues or rules.

## Assumptions (recorded, to be confirmed in C1)

- `LevelDefinition` / `WaveDefinition` / `WaveGroup` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`) are already fully serialisable and sufficient to express "the enemies to appear, the level and wave numbers".
- `Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` and `Player.getPowerUpLevelStore().collect(id, permanent)` are the correct shared loadout seams; power-up ids self-validate via `getPowerUpById`.
- `applyEnemyCountScaling` means a configured group `count` is a *base* count that level scaling then transforms — the schema must state whether configured counts are pre- or post-scaling.
- Seeding the shared RNG for the duration of a capture is sufficient for reproducibility; audio-visual jitter outside RNG (frame timing) is acceptable.

## Existing state / key files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` — pure multi-scene core: `parseSceneConfig`, `loadSceneConfig`, `buildScenePlan`, `SCENE_CONFIG_ERROR_CODES`, `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS`, `PARAMETERISED_GYM_SCENE_KEYS`, payload builder.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` / `.d.mts` — hermetic contract tests and types; registry pinned against `src/scenes/gym/` on disk.
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` — dev-gated `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector.start(key)`; `resolveSceneKey` validates against the shared registry plus page discovery.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — already accepts `{ waves, levelName }` / `{ level }`; hard-codes spread+dual at start.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — `init({ enemyKey })`; resolves config via `loadEnemyConfig`.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — shared base for the formation gyms (roster/loadout seams).
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — `LevelDefinition`, `WaveDefinition`, `WaveGroup`, `LEVELS`.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `equipWeapon`, `resetWeapon`, `getPowerUpLevelStore`.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore.collect`.
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `createSeededRng`, `normaliseSeed`, `randomSeed`.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `--scenes` mode: boot, recorder, fade overlay, probes, `--json`.
- `examples/scenes.json`, `README.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **Scripted Gameplay Videos (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC)** — `completed`. The multi-scene capture foundation this extends.
- **Dev-gated in-page capture scene director (AH-0MVFC6WPS004UOLO)** — `completed`. Currently key-only; AC3 extends it.
- **Pure scene-capture module (AH-0MVFC6TCY005E39P)** — `completed`. Where the setup schema and validation land.
- **Scripted Gameplay Videos: generated-level scenes (Option C follow-up) (AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX)** — `idea`. Blocked by this epic's setup pass-through; dependency edge recorded.
- **Compile an action video (AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX)** — `open`. Consumes captured footage; a setup-bearing capture gives it better material.
data.title: Config-defined scene setups for scripted gameplay capture

# C1 — Setup schema, defaults and fail-fast validation (test-first)

Child of Config-defined scene setups for scripted gameplay capture (AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6). Parent ACs: AC1, AC2 (and AC6 defaults half).

## Summary

Define, in the pure browser-free module `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`, the `setup` schema a `scenes.json` entry may carry, its documented defaults, its normalisation, and fail-fast validation with stable machine-readable error codes. Tests first (red), then the implementation. No browser, no `src/` changes.

## User story

As the maintainer, a typo (unknown enemy, bad wave index, unknown power-up id) fails in milliseconds with an actionable message naming the offending scene entry and field, instead of booting Chromium and recording the wrong thing.

## Scope

- Extend the parsed scene-entry shape with an optional `setup` object. When absent, the parsed entry and every downstream artefact must be **identical** to today's (add an explicit unchanged-behaviour test).
- Model the setup as: level (`LevelDefinition`-shaped: `level`, `name`, `waves[]` with `groups[]` and the existing opt-in flags `shootEnabled` / `ghosts` / `centipede` / `horde` / `laneTraffic` / `miniBoss`), a starting wave index, an enemy key for formation gyms, the player loadout (permanent and timed weapon ids), power-up levels by id, and a `seed`.
- Normalisation fills documented defaults (e.g. default weapon set when `player` is omitted, default seed, default starting wave) and drops nothing silently.
- Validation rejects, with new codes in `SCENE_CONFIG_ERROR_CODES`: unknown field, wrong type, unknown `enemyKey`, unknown formation kind, unknown weapon id, unknown power-up id, level/wave index out of range, missing required parameter for a parameterised target (`GymLevel` / `GymFodderEnemies`), and a setup supplied to a target that cannot accept one.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests exist **first** and cover: absent-setup unchanged behaviour; each new error code; defaults filled by normalisation; idempotent normalisation (normalise(normalise(x)) deep-equals normalise(x)); setup preserved per entry in file order alongside the existing timing fields.
- Error messages name the scene index and field; codes (not wording) are asserted.
- The module still imports nothing (no Node APIs, no DOM, no Vite) so both the CLI and the in-page director can import it.
- Types are extended in `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` and typecheck cleanly.
- The existing registry-pinning test and `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` still pass.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts`
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` (consumer; read-only here)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (error-code table; prose lands in C5)

## Minimal implementation

Add `parseSceneSetup` / `normaliseSceneSetup` / `validateSceneSetup` pure functions and a `SCENE_SETUP_FIELD_SPECS` style table, mirroring the existing `parseSceneConfig` structure and error-code discipline. Valid ids are resolved from the existing shared registries (`loadEnemyConfig` keys, `WeaponId`, `getPowerUpById`) via dependency injection or a frozen mirrored list with a parity test — do **not** hand-copy a drifting list.

## Dependencies

None (first item). Everything else consumes this contract.

## Deliverables

Schema + defaults + validation + types + tests, all hermetic.

# C2 — Director and registry: pass setup through `start(key, setup)`

Child of Config-defined scene setups for scripted gameplay capture (AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6). Parent ACs: AC3.

## Summary

Make the dev-only in-page capture director accept launch data and forward it into the target scene, and gate the previously rejected parameterised gyms on the presence of a valid setup — so `GymLevel` and `GymFodderEnemies` become recordable without any page navigation.

## User story

As the maintainer, I can record `GymLevel` and `GymFodderEnemies` in a multi-scene capture by supplying their setup in `scenes.json`, and the single `MediaRecorder` keeps rolling across the switch.

## Scope

- `start(key, setup?)` forwards the (already normalised) setup as `scene.start(key, setup)` through the existing scene-manager path.
- `resolveSceneKey` / `startScene` gating: a key in `PARAMETERISED_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` is accepted **only** with a setup that satisfies its required parameter, and rejected otherwise with the shared error code. Non-parameterised keys keep today's behaviour; an unexpected setup on a target that cannot consume it is rejected consistently with C1.
- Update `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` semantics (or introduce the accessor that resolves "watchable given this setup") so the CLI pre-boot validation and the director guard stay a single source of truth, and the registry pinning test against `src/scenes/gym/` on disk is updated deliberately.
- Capture driver (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` `--scenes` mode) passes each entry's setup to the director call and reports the normalised setup in the `--json` payload (AC6).

## Acceptance criteria

- A test proves `start(key, setup)` reaches the scene manager as `start(key, <normalised setup>)` and that no navigation/reload occurs (director fake, no browser).
- `GymLevel` without setup ⇒ rejected; with a valid setup ⇒ accepted. Same for `GymFodderEnemies` (`enemy` key). Both assertions made for **both** the CLI validation path and the director path, so the two can never disagree.
- The registry/deviation is documented in code comments, and the pinning test fails if a gym scene is added or removed without updating the registry.
- Dev gate unchanged: `isCaptureDirectorEnabled()` is constant `false` in a production build and `npm run check-bundle` stays green.
- The `--json` payload exposes, per scene, the normalised setup alongside the existing timing fields.

## Key Files

- `src/core/captureDirector.ts`
- `src/core/captureDirector.test.ts`
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` (registry/validation accessors)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts`
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (`--scenes` mode wiring + payload)
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`

## Minimal implementation

Thread a `setup` argument through `startScene` → `SceneManagerLike.start(key, setup)`; add a `resolveWatchableSceneEntry(entry)` that returns the resolved key plus normalised setup, used by both the CLI's pre-boot loop and the director. Keep the existing structural `SceneManagerLike` interfaces so tests stay browser-free.

## Dependencies

- C1 — setup schema, defaults and validation.

## Deliverables

Director pass-through + gated registry + CLI wiring + payload field + hermetic tests.

# C3 — Shared setup application helper and gym integration

Child of Config-defined scene setups for scripted gameplay capture (AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6). Parent ACs: AC4 (and the loadout/level half of AC1).

## Summary

Add one shared helper that turns a normalised setup into play state using only existing shared seams, and wire it into the gym scenes' `init`/`create` so the configured state is live **before** the first captured frame (i.e. during the `playMs` warm-up).

## User story

As a viewer of a showcase clip, the very first frame of each scene already shows the configured loadout and the configured enemies — no dead frames while a scene "catches up".

## Scope

- New shared helper (suggested `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) with a pure-ish `applySceneSetup(scene seams, setup)` entry point:
  - level hand-off: supply the `LevelDefinition` and starting wave to the wave loop (`GymLevel`'s documented `{ level }` / `{ waves, levelName }` launch contract);
  - player loadout: `equipWeapon(id, true)` for configured permanent weapons, `equipWeapon(id, false)` + timer for configured timed weapons, and `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)` for configured power-up levels;
  - formation-gym enemy selection: the `enemyKey` seam `GymFodderEnemies.init` already uses, generalised to the formation gyms that can accept it.
- Wire it into `GymLevel`, `GymFodderEnemies` and `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms at the earliest safe point (before wave scheduling and before the supply layer's first tick), preserving current behaviour when no setup is supplied.
- Replace `GymLevel`'s hard-coded spread+dual with a **default** that the helper reproduces exactly, so today's behaviour is unchanged when `player` is omitted.
- Keep the helper the *only* place that knows how a setup becomes play state (no per-scene copies of the mapping).

## Acceptance criteria

- A test asserts the same state after applying a setup: expected active weapon ids (`getActiveWeapons`), weapon levels, power-up effective levels, and the launched wave list for a configured level + starting wave.
- With no setup, `GymLevel` / `GymFodderEnemies` / formation gyms produce exactly their pre-change state (explicit unchanged-behaviour test per scene touched).
- Setup is applied before the first recorded frame: an integration test drives the warm-up then asserts the captured-window start state matches the setup (no first-frame blank/dead state).
- **Parity preserved:** `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard stays green; the helper contains no gameplay logic that is duplicated from `PlayScene`.
- Any intentional divergence (e.g. a gym that cannot accept a level because it has no campaign-level input, which `GymLevel`'s header already documents for `GymFormationScene`) is recorded in the work item and in a code comment next to the divergence.
- Typecheck, build and the changed-scope tests pass.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` (new) + `.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts`, `GymFodderEnemies.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (guard must stay green)
- `src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` (consumed, not changed)
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` (consumed, not changed)

## Minimal implementation

One function taking narrow structural seams (`getPlayer()`, `equipWeapon`, wave-queue hand-off) so it is unit-testable with fakes and identical in gyms and (later) other scenes. Explicitly **no** scene-class generation.

## Dependencies

- C1 — setup schema, defaults and validation.

## Deliverables

Shared applier + gym wiring + unchanged-behaviour and applied-state tests.

# C4 — Seeded determinism contract for setup-driven randomness

Child of Config-defined scene setups for scripted gameplay capture (AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6). Parent AC: AC5.

## Summary

Make setup-driven randomness reproducible from the config's `seed`, so the same `scenes.json` produces the same scene content on every run, and report the resolved seed in the `--json` payload.

## User story

As the maintainer, I can re-record a clip after a balance change and get the same enemy placement and drop sequence, so the only visible difference is the change I made.

## Scope

- Identify every randomness source that affects a configured scene's *content* (formation placement / start ranges, drop spawner cadence, mineral seeding, generated enemies, any scene-local `Math.random`).
- Route those sources through the existing shared `createSeededRng` / `normaliseSeed` (`src/core/rng.ts`) when a setup supplies a seed (or a documented default seed), without changing behaviour when no setup is supplied.
- Report the resolved seed (explicit or defaulted) in the `--json` payload per scene, and document the reproducibility guarantee **and its limits** (frame-timing/encoder jitter is out of scope; content determinism is in scope).

## Acceptance criteria

- A test asserts two runs with the same seed produce identical derived content (spawn positions, enemy keys/counts, drop sequence), and different seeds produce different content for at least one asserted axis.
- A test asserts that an entry **without** `setup` behaves exactly as today (no RNG re-plumbing side effects).
- No `Math.random` remains on a configured scene's content path (asserted by a scan test or by construction + a comment), and the shared RNG is the single source.
- Resolved seed is present in the `--json` payload and documented in the schema docs (prose in C5).
- Full suite and build green.

## Key Files

- `src/core/rng.ts` (consumed)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts`, `GymFodderEnemies.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` (seed hand-off)
- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` + `.test.ts` (seed defaulting/normalisation)
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (prose in C5)

## Minimal implementation

Thread the seed through the same setup object C1 normalises and C3 applies; seed at the earliest scene-lifecycle point so every later draw is deterministic. Keep the RNG injectable so tests need no browser.

## Dependencies

- C3 — shared setup application helper and gym integration.

## Deliverables

Seeded content path + seed reporting + determinism tests + limits documented.

# Capture director does not stop the previously running scene (scene stacking)

The dev-gated in-page capture director starts each requested capture scene with
`scene.start(key)` and never stops the scene that is already running, so every
previously started scene keeps updating (and emitting audio) for the rest of
the recording — and because `PlayScene` is registered before any lazily added
gym scene, the newest scene can render *underneath* a stale one. Starting a
capture scene must stop every other running scene first, so exactly one capture
scene runs and the requested scene is the visible one.

## Problem statement

`startScene()` (`src/core/captureDirector.ts`, AH-0MVFC6WPS004UOLO) resolves and
registers the requested gym scene, then calls `manager.start(key)`. Phaser's
`SceneManager.start()` only shuts down and restarts the **target** scene
(`node_modules/phaser/src/scene/SceneManager.js` — `sys.shutdown()`/`sys.start()`
on the requested scene only); it never stops whatever else is running. So the
multi-scene capture of AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC / AH-0MVFC70GT000B96J leaves **every
previously started scene alive** behind the newest one: their `update` loops,
timers, spawners and audio keep ticking until the page closes.

It has gone unnoticed because gym scenes each fill the whole 960×540 canvas and
Phaser renders in registration order, so the most recently *added* gym scene
draws on top and the footage looks right. The costs are hidden: wasted CPU
across stacked scenes (a soak/stability risk on long recordings) and SFX from
scenes that are supposed to be finished mixed into the shared `AudioContext`
the recorder taps.

It becomes a **hard blocker** for generated-level scenes (AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX):
`PlayScene` is registered in `gameConfig.scene` at boot — *before* any
lazily-added gym scene — so starting a generated level after a gym scene would
render the level **underneath** the still-running gym and record the wrong
scene.

The **very first** switch is already affected: the capture pipeline presses
Enter to satisfy the autoplay policy, which starts `PlayScene`, and the director
then starts the first gym scene on top of it. The first recorded scene is
therefore already a stack.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner compiling showcase videos.**
  As the maintainer, I can put any mix of capture scenes in one scene list
  (gym → gym, gym → generated level, level → gym) and the recorded clip shows
  the scene I asked for, with no invisible scene still running behind it, so
  long recordings stay cheap and the footage stays trustworthy.
- **Secondary — future capture-scene authors (Option C generated levels).**
  As a developer adding a new capture target, I can rely on a single documented
  invariant ("exactly one capture scene runs") instead of having to reason
  about Phaser's registration order for my target.
- **Secondary — the audience of the showcase clips.** They should see only the
  scene being showcased: no stray SFX from a scene that has already ended and
  no under-layer bleeding through a partially transparent scene.

## Existing state

- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` exposes `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector`
  (`start(key)`) in dev builds only, and is inert in production
  (`import.meta.env.DEV` gate; `npm run check-bundle` asserts this).
- `startScene(game, key)` validates the key against the shared watchable
  registry (`scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`) plus page discovery, registers the
  gym scene class if needed (`manager.add`), then calls `manager.start(key)`.
- `SceneManagerLike` (`getScene`, `add`, `start`) is the structural seam that
  lets `src/core/captureDirector.test.ts` drive a fake scene manager with no
  browser.
- The multi-scene driver (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, `driveSceneSequence`)
  keeps one page and one `MediaRecorder`, fading to black between scenes and
  calling the director's `start(key)` per scene.
- Phaser 3 details confirmed in `node_modules/phaser/src/scene/`:
  - `SceneManager.start(key)` shuts down only `key`.
  - `SceneManager.stop(key)` sets `active = false`, `visible = false` and emits
    `SHUTDOWN` (it also unloads the scene's loader listeners).
  - `SceneManager.getScenes(true)` returns the **active** scenes, so "who else
    is running?" is answerable without extra bookkeeping.
  - `SceneManager.bringToTop(key)` reorders the render list, and scene-manager
    ops issued while the manager is processing are queued (`queueOp`).
  - The `SoundManager` is **one global instance shared by all scenes**
    (`Systems#sound` is "the global Sound Manager"), so stopping a scene does
    *not* silence sounds it already started.

## Desired change

Before starting the requested scene, the director stops **every active scene
other than the target**, then starts the target and brings it to the top.

Sequence per `start(key)` call: resolve/validate key → register class if absent
→ stop all currently active scenes except `key` → `start(key)` →
`bringToTop(key)`.

This gives one documented invariant: after any director `start(key)`, the only
active scene is `key`, and `key` is the top-most scene — independent of
registration order and independent of which scene happened to be running
before (the warm-up `PlayScene`, `GymIndex`, another gym, or nothing).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — the previous scene is stopped before the next starts.** A hermetic
  director test (fake scene manager, no browser) proves that for a switch from
  scene A to scene B, `stop(A)` happens *before* `start(B)`, and that the
  manager is left with exactly one active scene (the target).
- **AC2 — the very first switch is single-scene too.** A hermetic test seeds
  the fake manager with a boot-registered running scene (`PlayScene`, added
  before the target) and asserts the director stops it, so the first scene of a
  recording is not stacked either.
- **AC3 — the started scene is the top-most/visible one regardless of
  registration order.** A test pins that after a switch whose registration
  order differs (boot-registered `PlayScene` vs. lazily added gym scene) the
  target is the top-most scene (`bringToTop`/last-rendered), covering
  gym → gym, gym → boot-registered scene and gym → lazily added scene.
- **AC4 — no navigation or reload; one page, one recorder.** The existing
  no-navigation guarantees still hold for the switch path (only the scene
  manager is touched; no `location` write, no reload), and the multi-scene
  driver still runs one page and one `MediaRecorder` across all switches (no
  regression in `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`).
- **AC5 — re-starting a stopped scene starts it clean.** A test pins that a
  scene previously stopped by the director is started afresh (stop → start
  ordering via the manager, no reuse of a paused/slept instance), so a repeated
  scene key records a fresh run.
- **AC6 — invalid keys keep failing loudly and touch nothing.** The existing
  typed `SceneConfigError` rejections (unknown, blank, parameterised,
  registry/disk divergence) still throw *before* any stop/start call on the
  manager.
- **AC7 — documented.** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` states the
  one-scene-at-a-time and top-most guarantees in the multi-scene "How it works"
  section; `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` asserts that text so the doc
  cannot silently drift from the code; the `startScene` / `SceneManagerLike`
  JSDoc states the invariant; `README.md` is updated if the guarantee is worth
  a line in the capture blurb; any other related docs are updated.
- **AC8 — production stays inert.** `npm run check-bundle` passes; the new code
  sits behind the existing `import.meta.env.DEV` gate and adds no production
  bytes that survive dead-code elimination.
- **AC9 — the full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Behaviour-preserving elsewhere.** No gameplay behaviour change; the only
  behaviour that changes is the capture director's scene lifecycle, and only in
  dev builds.
- **Keep the director hermetic-testable.** Extend `SceneManagerLike`
  structurally (e.g. `stop`, `getScenes`, `bringToTop`) so the existing fake
  scene manager still tests the whole path with no browser and no real Phaser.
- **Stay inside the existing seams.** No new dependencies, no changes to
  `gameConfig`, no changes to scene registration order, no changes to
  `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`'s watchable registry.
- **Merge order with C2.** "Director and registry: pass setup through
  `start(key, setup)`" (AH-0MVNW8UCZ004CY0R) touches the same file; whichever
  lands second rebases on the other rather than developing in parallel.
- **Scope guard.** Do not extend the fix into generated-level capture. Deliberate
  non-goals: silencing in-flight audio with `game.sound.stopAll()` (would cut a
  scene's SFX tails mid-fade and is a separate fidelity decision), pausing with
  `sleep()` instead of `stop()`, and any rendering/resolution change. Extra
  opportunities found while implementing are filed as separate linked work
  items, not folded in.

## Decisions and assumptions (recorded, no producer input required)

- **`stop()`, not `sleep()`.** `stop()` deactivates the scene
  (`active`/`visible` false, `SHUTDOWN` emitted) and forces a fresh
  `init`/`create` next time, which is what a showcase wants; `sleep()` keeps the
  scene's state and display list, and `start()` on a slept scene resumes
  mid-run state — a second appearance of the same gym would then show a
  half-finished run. It also leaves the scene registered as active, so
  "exactly one active scene" would not hold.
- **Stop *all* active scenes except the target, not just the previous capture
  scene.** The director keeps no history, and the very first switch already has
  a scene it did not start (the warm-up `PlayScene`). Stopping by observation
  (`getScenes(true)`) covers both cases with one rule.
- **`bringToTop()` after `start()`.** With every other scene stopped, ordering
  should be moot; the explicit call makes the visible-scene guarantee
  independent of Phaser's op queueing (`queueOp` while the manager is
  processing) and of `Game`'s scene array order.
- **Stop is safe for the boot scenes too.** Every scene in `gameConfig.scene`
  (`MenuScene`, `PlayScene`, `PauseScene`, `HelpScene`, `MineralChoiceScene`,
  `SettingsScene`, `TelemetryConsentScene`, `GameOverScene`,
  `LeaderboardScene`, `GymIndex`) is a navigation scene, not a persistent
  HUD/overlay; there is no always-on scene that must survive a switch.
- **Audio leakage is bounded, not eliminated.** Verified in
  `node_modules/phaser/src/sound/`: one global `SoundManager` is shared by all
  scenes, and no scene has a shutdown handler stopping sound — so sounds
  already playing when the scene stops are not cut. `grep "loop: true"` finds
  no looping audio in `src/`, so residual leakage is limited to in-flight
  one-shot SFX (≤ their duration). Eliminating that is recorded as a non-goal
  above.
- **Priority `high` (operator-set, kept).** It blocks
  AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX (dependency edge already recorded).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` — Needs `SceneManagerLike` extended with
  `stop`, `getScenes` and `bringToTop`, and `startScene` to stop all other
  active scenes before starting (and bring the target to the top); JSDoc update
  stating the one-scene/top-most invariant.
- `src/core/captureDirector.test.ts` — Needs the new hermetic tests (AC1–AC6)
  and an extended fake scene manager recording stop/start/bringToTop order.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — Needs the one-scene-at-a-time guarantee in
  the multi-scene "How it works" section (§ Multi-scene capture).
- `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` — Needs a docs assertion for that
  guarantee (keeps doc and code in step).
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — Expected to need **no** change; only
  inspected, to confirm the driver keeps one page/one `MediaRecorder` and no
  reload (AC4). Its page-side call site is the only consumer of `start(key)`.
- `README.md` — Only if the guarantee is worth a line in the capture blurb
  (it already cross-links `capture:scenes`); likely no change.
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-capture-director-scene-stacking-AH-0MVNWJ5FH006QD8V.md`
  — this intake brief (temporary; removed after the intake finishes).

## Risks and mitigations

- **Risk: stopping a boot scene has a side effect we have not seen in a real
  recording.** Mitigation: the recording pipeline is verified by an actual
  `npm run capture:scenes` run in implementation review; the unit tests pin the
  manager protocol, the manual capture confirms the footage.
- **Risk: an always-on overlay scene is added later and gets stopped.**
  Mitigation: state the invariant in the code JSDoc and in
  `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, so a future overlay author sees that capture
  switches stop every non-target scene.
- **Risk: fake-manager tests pass while real Phaser defers the stop (op queue).**
  Mitigation: keep `bringToTop` and assert protocol order; note the `queueOp`
  behaviour in a code comment.
- **Risk: merge conflict with the C2 setup work (AH-0MVNW8UCZ004CY0R).**
  Mitigation: land second, rebase, re-run the director tests.
- **Risk: scope creep into generated-level capture / audio fidelity.**
  Mitigation: explicit non-goals above; new opportunities become linked work
  items.

## Related work

- **Scripted Gameplay Videos** (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC) — parent feature this bug
  was found under.
- **Dev-gated in-page capture scene director** (AH-0MVFC6WPS004UOLO) — the
  module being fixed.
- **Multi-scene capture driver: one recorder, fades, single WebM**
  (AH-0MVFC70GT000B96J) — the driver that calls `start(key)` and must keep one
  page/one recorder (AC4).
- **Scripted Gameplay Videos: generated-level scenes (Option C follow-up)**
  (AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX) — **blocked by this item** (dependency edge);
  `PlayScene` vs. lazily added gym registration order is exactly its blocker.
- **Config-defined scene setups for scripted gameplay capture**
  (AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6) and its child C2 **Director and registry: pass setup
  through `start(key, setup)`** (AH-0MVNW8UCZ004CY0R) — same file, merge-order
  coordination.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` § Multi-scene capture; § Known limits → Audio
  capture.

### Related work (automated report, curated)

`/skill:find-related` was run for this item. Work-item matches worth keeping:
**AH-0MVFC70GT000B96J** (completed, the driver that calls `start(key)`) and
**AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX** (blocked on this item). Its third match,
AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD (crash-resilient telemetry upload), is unrelated to scene
lifecycle and was dropped per the conservative-report policy; the repository
file matches were generic keyword noise (`README.md`, the GDD and
`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` match on common prose words) and were
dropped too. The untruncated report is kept at
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MVNWJ5FH006QD8V.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**No producer questions were required.** The seed description for
AH-0MVNWJ5FH006QD8V already contained a problem statement, expected behaviour
and five acceptance criteria, and the remaining open points were answerable from
the repository (Phaser sources, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, the existing
director tests). Every decision taken is recorded above, each with its evidence,
for producer review at the review stage.

- **Q: Stop or sleep the previous scene?** — Answer (agent, from evidence):
  **stop**. `SceneManager.stop()` deactivates the scene and emits `SHUTDOWN`,
  so the next `start()` runs a fresh `init`/`create`; `sleep()` keeps the
  display list and state and leaves the scene counted as active. Evidence:
  `node_modules/phaser/src/scene/SceneManager.js` (`start`, `stop`),
  `src/scene/Systems.js` (`shutdown`). Source: repository inspection.
- **Q: Which scenes must be stopped — only ones the director started, or all
  active scenes?** — Answer (agent): **all active scenes except the target**.
  The first switch in every capture already runs on top of the `PlayScene`
  started by the warm-up Enter press (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, ~line
  2139), and the director keeps no history. Evidence:
  `SceneManager.getScenes(true)` returns active scenes; `gameConfig.scene` has
  no always-on overlay. Source: repository inspection.
- **Q: Does stopping a scene stop its audio?** — Answer (agent): **no**, Phaser
  has one global `SoundManager` shared by all scenes and no scene here stops
  its sounds on shutdown, so in-flight one-shots are not cut (no `loop: true`
  audio exists in `src/`, so leakage is bounded). Recorded as a non-goal;
  evidence: `node_modules/phaser/src/scene/Systems.js` (`Systems#sound` is
  "the global Sound Manager"), `node_modules/phaser/src/sound/SoundManagerCreator.js`.
  Source: repository inspection.
- **Q: Does an overlapping work item already cover this?** — Answer (agent):
  **no**. Duplicate check performed (`wl search` on "capture director", "scene
  manager stop", "capture scene stacking", "bringToTop"): the only overlapping
  items are the completed director/driver work and the blocked Option C item
  that this item unblocks. Source: worklog search.
data.title: Capture director does not stop the previously running scene (scene stacking)

Discovered during intake of AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14 (discovered-from:AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14).

Follow-up from the producer's Q1 decision (a spent force-field bubble dims rather than vanishing): a permanent (hold-full) Force Field currently never regenerates its reflect budget (_forceFieldRemaining), so after the base 3 reflections it is dim (per the new spent-dim visual) and purely decorative for the rest of the run.

User story: As a player, I want a permanent Force Field to keep earning reflections over time (cf. the Thorn Field recharge, AH-0MVJ8YKR70096C6T), so the hold-full reward stays useful.

Acceptance criteria:
- A permanent Force Field regenerates reflections over time (interval resolved from level, cf. thorns recharge) up to its resolved budget.
- Regeneration drives the bubble from the spent-dim state back to the active look (visual follow-through from AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14).
- Regeneration applies in the game and every gym via the shared registry tick (gym-game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- Unit tests cover regeneration timing, the budget cap and the dim-to-active visual transition.
- Docs (GDD force_field row, HUD/help copy mentioning the budget) updated; full suite passes.

Out of scope for AH-0MVBKT2WO001AR14 — tracked separately so its dim state does not permanently neuter the permanent reward.

# In-page fallback probe inflates node RSS above the <512 MiB budget

Discovered during **AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES** (verify fix with full suite and a
manual long-run soak), discovered-from **AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE**.

## Observation

A 5-clip full-run soak (`--count 5 --max-duration 1800000 --diagnostics`,
output written to `/tmp/ah-soak/`) completed every clip, but the process node
RSS peaked at **661.0 MiB** (clip 4 start) — above the documented **< 512 MiB**
target. The peak is not recording growth: it is `peakRssBytes` at the *start*
of a clip, carried over from the **previous** clip's end-of-clip probe, and
every clip's end-of-recording RSS was 320–388 MiB.

Cause: clips 3 (34.9 MiB) and 5 (62.75 MiB) are above the 32 MiB in-page probe
threshold, but their files sat outside the served repository root
(`/tmp/ah-soak/…`), so the probe fell back to the **in-page Blob** path
(documented fallback, reported by `probeSourceReason`). That fallback decodes
up to the 32 MiB retained prefix with `decodeAudioData` in one shot, which
inflates node RSS by a few hundred MiB temporarily. A control run of the same
workload with the output inside the repo root (`capture-output/soak/`,
600 s, 48.43 MiB) used the **streamed** probe and peaked at only **408.9 MiB**.

## Why it matters

The < 512 MiB budget is documented for a full-cap run, and `--output /tmp/…`
is a supported, documented invocation. The *path*-based fallback (and its RSS
cost) is not covered by the parent's stated fallback rationale, which only
sanctions the in-page decode for clips *below* a size threshold.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Document, in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` §Long-run memory budget, that
   the streamed probe needs the output inside the served repository root and
   that the in-page fallback costs a temporary whole-prefix audio decode
   (with the measured 661 MiB batch peak vs 408.9 MiB streamed as the
   evidence), or
2. Make the streamed probe work for outputs outside the served root (e.g. a
   temporary route serving the partial file), restoring the < 512 MiB budget
   for every supported output path.
3. Re-run a > 32 MiB clip with `--output /tmp/…` and record the peak RSS
   against the budget.

## Evidence

Full numbers, per-clip diagnostics and logs: comment on
AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES; diagnostics artefacts under `/tmp/ah-soak/`
(`batch-1..5.diagnostics.json`) and
`capture-output/soak/soak-streamed2.diagnostics.json`.
data.title: In-page fallback probe inflates node RSS above the <512 MiB budget for long clips written outside the served repo root

# Flaky PlayScene integration test

Discovered during **AH-0MVNT2CD3001I8ES** (verify fix with full suite), from **AH-0MVN06MS9007LRKE**.

`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` failed once in three full-suite executions at the same commit (08891f72):

- 23:35 worktree run: **pass** (7010/7010)
- 01:19 main-checkout run (parallel with 3 other repos' full suites on the host): **fail** (1/7010; 106 ms, Phaser Canvas boot log only, no assertion detail captured by the runner)
- 01:26 forced fresh main-checkout run: **pass** (7010/7010)

Verdict: flaky under host load, not a code regression (the fix series touched dev tooling only, not `PlayScene`).

ACs:
1. Rerun the test 5× in isolation (or under load) and confirm the failure rate and cause; fix or quarantine if it reproduces.
2. Either make the assertion load-robust (e.g. frame-budget polling) or document the known flake in the test file; declare the verdict on this item.

data.description: All gym scenes should behave exactly as the main gameplay scene does. Right now at least the Bot tuning scene does not (you should check all others too). There are a number of fixes from the main game that do not appear in the bot tuning scene. For example, the phasers do not have the fix that sees them spawn from the wormhole in formation, instead they appear as a line then snap to a circle formation after all have spawned. This implies we need to refactor the gym scenes to remove dead code and ensure they behave the same as the main scene. We should also consider that the work to create scriptable videos is expanding how we define scripted scenes. It might make sense to configure all gym scenes to use this feature.

data.description: Create descriptions for the example scripted video that follow a curve of excitement such that the openeing scene has many enemies, lots of minerals and upgrades, the player has all six upgrade slots filled with level 2-5 weapons. The second scene should be an early scene with a player that only has the default weapon, the wormhole spawns a few weak enemies but there are lots of asteroids for the player to destroy and collect. End the second scene with the player getting a Hull Full reward. The next scene will have about 2x the number of enemies, and 3 weapon slots filled with level 1 weapons. Then 2x the number of enemies again, with 5 slots filled with level 1-2 weapons. Next a mini-boss with a reasonable number of enemies, full slots with level 1-3 weapons. End this one with the death of the miniboss. Then back to something similar to the 4th scene (different enemies more player weapons) then finally the main boss with loads of weapons, end with the death of the boss.
